groups.title: Security guides and write-ups
groups.intro: Almost all of these are about window.postMessage listeners that do not check who sent the message. A private MessagePort avoids that class of bug, because only the holder of the other end can send to it.

groups.title: Research papers: security of messaging
groups.intro: I found no paper that is only about MessageChannel. The research is about postMessage, frames and workers, and several papers cover ports as part of that.

items.t: Protection and Communication Abstractions for Web Browsers in MashupOS
items.by: Wang, Fan, Howell and Jackson, SOSP

items.by: Barth, Jackson and Mitchell, USENIX Security
items.n: Found a confidentiality flaw in the first postMessage design. The fix is the target origin argument used today.
Shows how libraries layered on postMessage and similar channels let one side compromise the other. PDF.

items.t: The Emperor's New APIs: On the (In)Secure Usage of New Client-side Primitives

items.t: The Postman Always Rings Twice: Attacking and Defending postMessage in HTML5 Websites
items.n: A study of message receivers on the Alexa top 10,000 sites. Many checked the origin incorrectly or not at all.

items.t: Protecting Users by Confining JavaScript with COWL
items.by: Stefan, Yang, Marchenko, Russo, Herman, Karp and Mazières, OSDI
items.n: Adds labels to browser contexts and to the messages they exchange, so a page can share data with code it does not trust.

items.t: ZigZag: Automatically Hardening Web Applications Against Client-side Validation Vulnerabilities
items.by: Weissbacher, Robertson, Kirda, Kruegel and Vigna, USENIX Security
items.n: Learns what normal messages look like and blocks ones that do not fit, to protect weak postMessage receivers.

items.t: How the Web Tangled Itself: Uncovering the History of Client-Side Web (In)Security
items.by: Stock, Johns, Steffens and Backes, USENIX Security
items.n: Twenty years of archived pages, including how postMessage use and missing origin checks grew over time.

items.t: Study and Mitigation of Origin Stripping Vulnerabilities in Hybrid-postMessage Enabled Mobile Applications
items.by: Yang, Huang, Gu and Mendoza, IEEE S&P

items.t: Site Isolation: Process Separation for Web Sites within the Browser
items.by: Reis, Moshchuk and Oskov, USENIX Security
items.n: How Chrome puts each site in its own process. Explains what it took to keep postMessage working between frames in different processes.

items.t: PMForce: Systematically Analyzing postMessage Handlers at Scale
items.n: Automated analysis of message handlers on the top 100,000 sites. It found 111 handlers it could exploit automatically.

items.t: Careful Who You Trust: Studying the Pitfalls of Cross-Origin Communication
items.by: Meiser, Laperdrix and Stock, ACM AsiaCCS
items.n: Maps which sites trust which others through postMessage and CORS, and how far a flaw in one site reaches.
